feature: Title pages that look like Apple designed them
summary: The ten title pages from the mock you picked are now the first title pages in the Library and the Insert menus, drawn and moving as the mock does; the old busy set waits under More Styles.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording.

try.do: Open the Library, press Catalog, and type Keynote in its search: Keynote Section sits under Title Pages, Keynote Clean under More Styles.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick the recording, then double click Keynote Section: it lands in front of the recording on V1 with a dissolve into it.
Type a headline and press Command Return.
Press Home and step a quarter second at a time: the word sharpens out of a soft focus, the line under it rises a few points.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Step on to two seconds: it holds perfectly still on black.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open Sequence > Insert Title Page: the ten are listed, then a More Styles submenu with the old pages.
Watch the reel of all ten: 2026-10-18-apple-titles-reel.mp4, and the mock beside the app: 2026-10-18-apple-titles-beside-mock.png.

evaluate: Would you put any of the ten in front of an Apple keynote audience without wincing?
Does any page still read as a school presentation? Which one, and what about it?
Is Editorial's serif, a little bolder and narrower than in the mock, acceptable?
Is More Styles the right place for the old pages, or should they go entirely once the toned down versions land?
Do the entrances feel calm rather than slow?
rough: Editorial's headline serif is the Mac's 128 point cut of New York, a little bolder and about 60 pixels narrower than the mock's browser drew it (mean difference 5.6 of 255 against 0.2 to 2.8 for the other nine): settled by decision title-pages-that-look-like-apple-designed-them-the-ten-title-pages-are-built-fr.

Sessions Stage's glow is a round light where the mock's is an oval, so it reaches a little less far down the frame; within 2.8 of 255 of the mock at every moment measured: covered by decision title-pages-that-look-like-apple-designed-them-the-ten-title-pages-are-built-fr.

Film Super's warm pool of light is round where the mock's is an oval; within 1.7 of 255 of the mock: covered by decision title-pages-that-look-like-apple-designed-them-the-ten-title-pages-are-built-fr.
The sample words are the mock's (Timeline, Record. Redline. Ship., Dana Zhou, and so on) rather than Your Title, so the tile shows the design as designed; typing replaces them as before.
Matches the mock: a page's background is there from its first frame. Over footage mid-edit it therefore cuts in, and a transition on the cut softens that.
The old pages under More Styles are still as busy as before; toning them down is the-existing-title-pages-are-toned-down-to-calm.
Typing new words into any title no longer adds a halo shadow to words that had none; the old set's words never meant to wear one either.
